competencies.description: The Artificial Intelligence Techniques competency encompasses the knowledge and skills required to develop, deploy, and manage AI-driven solutions, including machine learning algorithms, deep learning models, natural language processing (NLP), and generative AI systems. It covers the full AI pipeline from data preparation and model development to ethical considerations and model deployment.
indicators: Apply complex AI methodologies (e.g., convolutional neural networks (CNNs) and recurrent neural networks (RNNs)) to complex problems (e.g., those involving multiple types of data, high ethical risks, or large impacts from errors).
Design and build production-ready AI solutions, including large language models (LLMs) and generative AI systems.
Apply and fine-tune tree-based algorithms such as decision trees, logistic regression, or clustering techniques.
Develop and deploy machine learning pipelines for production.
Implement deployment strategies for AI systems, including monitoring and maintaining performance post-deployment.
Stay up to date with emerging AI techniques and assess their applicability to business problems.
Identify AI/data science trends and tools, and their potential impacts.
Identify all challenges (e.g., hallucination, bias, replication, etc.) and benefits of AI.
Monitor automated decisions post-implementation for unintended outcomes.
Monitor AI systems for health, bias, and data drift.
Architect and deploy multi-agent systems capable of reasoning, planning, and acting autonomously.
Design and implement data workflows that combine prompt chaining, routing, and evaluator-optimizer loops.

competencies.description: Code Management involves the systematic use of tools, practices, and methodologies to organize, version, document, and maintain source code in data science and artificial intelligence (AI) projects. It includes version control, modular code organization, documentation standards, and collaborative workflows to ensure code is reproducible, scalable, and maintainable.
indicators: Evaluate version control workflows to identify inefficiencies in large-scale coding projects involving multiple contributors.
Organize repository and packaging the code to ensure clean code and documentation management practices at the end of project development.
Develop and enforce coding standards and tests (e.g., PEP 8) for code reviews to maintain high-quality, reproducible code.
Mentor and coach to improve team proficiency in code management practices and ensure adherence to standards.
Apply and promote responsible AI practices in code development and maintenance.

competencies.description: Project Management in the context of data science involves planning, organizing, and overseeing data-driven projects from initiation to completion. It includes managing resources, timelines, and deliverables while ensuring that project goals align with business objectives. It also involves risk management, stakeholder communication, and iterative problem-solving throughout the project lifecycle.
indicators: Head the planning and structuring of complex data science projects, setting clear goals, objectives, and deliverables.
Manage project resources effectively, including personnel, budget, and tools, ensuring optimal allocation for project success.
Proactively identify and manage Advanced project risks (e.g., scope creep, major technical challenges), implementing solutions to mitigate potential issues.
Lead coordination between cross-functional teams (data scientists, engineers, business stakeholders) to ensure alignment of project goals and seamless execution.
Prioritize evidence-based knowledge/data over conjecture (e.g., in data storytelling).
Promote self-serve access by design.
Work in a multidisciplinary team to inform problem framing with data.
Consider data use at the outset of a project.
Set analysis goals collaboratively with stakeholders.
Obtain stakeholder agreement on assessment criteria before implementation.
Prototype solutions for demonstration in customer environments.
Test solutions with diverse data for inclusiveness by design.
Ensure that projects are accessible by design.

competencies.description: Knowledge and ability to design, define, construct, enhance, support, and maintain software associated with machine learning.
indicators: Design and implement functions and classes in Python or R, applying object-oriented programming principles.
Use libraries like Pandas, NumPy, or dplyr to perform data manipulation tasks such as cleaning, transforming, and aggregating data.
Write and implement basic unit tests and functions for quality assurance.
Provide drill down functionality in visualizations.

competencies.description: Data processing refers to the collection, cleaning, transformation, and manipulation of raw data into a format suitable for analysis and decision-making. It involves handling data from various sources, ensuring its quality, and making it ready for statistical analysis or machine learning models.
indicators: Combine multiple datasets from different sources using joins or merges based on common keys, handling inconsistencies in data structure.
Write scripts to automate common data cleaning tasks, such as removing duplicates, correcting data types, and normalizing values.
Process both structured data (e.g., databases, spreadsheets) and unstructured data (e.g., text, logs) for analysis.
Perform complex data manipulations and transformations (e.g., data aggregation, time series processing).
Specify needs regarding tools and infrastructure requirements (e.g., compute capacity).
Create and maintain structured metadata; cleaning and manipulating structured metadata.
Publish data in machine-readable format.
Review and analyze outliers and their role as a potential root cause for quality issues.
Retain/maintain original data for outcome comparison.
Prioritize high-value datasets for interoperability.
Provide transparent documentation and rationale for dataset fitness for use.
Apply agentic AI tools (e.g., LLMs, workflow orchestrators) to automate data ingestion, cleaning, and transformation.

competencies.description: Technical communication is the ability to effectively convey complex data and analytical insights to diverse audiences, ensuring clarity, accuracy, and relevance. This competency encompasses presenting information using appropriate visual and narrative techniques, adapting messaging to suit stakeholder needs, and linking data findings to organizational objectives. Strong technical communicators make data accessible and actionable, bridging the gap between technical analysis and business decision-making. Mastery of this skill empowers teams to drive informed strategies and foster collaboration across the organization.
indicators: Organize data insights into a clear, logical structure, ensuring the narrative flow is easy to follow and the key insights are highlighted.
Create complex visualizations (e.g., heatmaps, scatter plots, time series plots) to demonstrate trends, correlations, or distributions, providing more detailed insights for specific audiences.
Adapt communication approach for different stakeholders (e.g., technical team vs. business Leaders), ensuring that the level of complexity is appropriate for the audience.
Develop data-driven narratives that directly link findings to business objectives, demonstrating how the insights impact strategy and decision-making.
Communicate risks of AI-generated content (e.g., copyright, bias, etc.).
